title_ru: JANUS Titan — ветвящаяся эволюция ядра, модульная экосистема и оптимизаторные трассы
analysis_method: Archive was extracted locally through libarchive with absolute-path and parent-traversal rejection.
Python source was parsed with ast.parse; JSON, CSV, SQLite schema, and text were inspected statically.
No Python, batch file, bytecode, database logic, optimizer, model, web server, or module was executed.
Credential-shaped values, private endpoints, free-form memory, logs, raw benchmark rows, and executable artifacts were not admitted.
core_findings: The archive contains 1000 files but only 451 unique contents; 549 files are exact duplicate copies.
A standalone JANUS core v115.1 and 19 janus_core snapshot directories represent two related but distinct architecture branches.
The 19 snapshot directories contain 11 distinct core.py contents and four distinct server.py contents; timestamp order is not a monotonic semantic-version order.
The modules tree is duplicated exactly under the backup directory, so 540 archived module files reduce to one 270-file ecosystem.
Benchmark and optimizer sources preserve a concrete experimental lineage with matching CSV/JSON logs, but no dataset or independent replay establishes model quality.
The archive contains multiple credential stores and private operational data and therefore cannot be published raw.
boundaries: This capsule proves artifact presence, chronology, hashes, and static structure only.
Terms such as sovereign, autonomy, quantum, tachyon, homeostasis, entropy, and evolution retain producer naming and are not independently validated scientific or cognitive claims.
A syntactically valid module is not safe to import or execute.
Internal benchmark scores are not external benchmarks and do not establish generalization.
Nothing in this capsule establishes consciousness, autonomous agency, quantum computation, or a result about P versus NP.
The raw archive is not committed.
